title: Bamberg World Heritage Run
short_description:
This tour is less for runners chasing their personal best and more for those who want to see some of Bamberg's beautiful old town while jogging.

The World Heritage Run has been held in Bamberg every two years since 2003. Its historical predecessors are the relay race "Quer durch Bamberg" and the "Bamberg Stadtlauf". This city-running course is one of the most demanding but also undoubtedly one of the most beautiful in all of Germany. In addition to the wonderful scenic highlights of the World Heritage Run, it is primarily the cultural and historical sights that make the World Heritage Run an unforgettable experience. The starting point of the tour is St. Mark's Square. The St. Mark's House of the same name, the former hospital of the city of Bamberg, is home to a faculty of the University of Bamberg. Besides the monastery of St. Michael, which is situated high above the roofs of the city on the Michaelsberg, the cathedral square with its historic buildings is one of the absolute highlights of this tour. But the Laupassagen along the Regnitz and through the Theresienhain also have their own special charm. The last kilometres of the route take us through the beautiful alleys of the city and across the Maxplatz, the central market and event location of the cathedral city.

The misty veil that shrouded the city slowly lifted, revealing a tapestry of Romanesque spires and Gothic facades. I took a deep breath, feeling the weight of centuries past as I set out to conquer the 12.3 kilometers that would lead me through the heart of this medieval gem.

The rhythmic pounding of my footsteps had become one with the city's heartbeat, and I felt a deep connection to the storied past that permeated every step. With each turn, I uncovered hidden gems: the majestic Imperial Cathedral, the picturesque streets of Little Venice, and the quaint charm of the old town. My run through Bamberg's World Heritage sites had become a testament to the city's enduring legacy.

title: Wiesn route in Munich
short_description:
During Oktoberfest, this is the most important route for many people. We experience the festival tents, the Bavaria statue, and can find up to six million new friends or even the love of our life.

This cheerful route takes us through Oktoberfest. We walk past the impressive festival tents and should decide early on for one or the other. The “stopover” becomes already problematic on weekends from 11 a.m. We should also not try to hop from one tent to the next and drink a beer everywhere. First, no one can handle one Maß per tent, and second, no cozy company can develop this way. And that is important. You realize this at the latest when, after the fourth Maß, you find yourself in the arms of the person to your left, making eternal friendship oaths or a marriage promise. Rides are dangerous. Unfortunately, for some, they only become interesting after a few beers. But that can end badly - literally. We better take a few carousel rounds before visiting a beer tent and then can focus calmly on the really important things in life: beer, atmosphere, roast chicken. The latter is a yearly point of contention, because on the one hand, half a roast chicken in the tents is usually immensely expensive, and on the other hand, there is probably nowhere else such a perfect roast chicken as at Wiesn. The same goes for the beer. Regardless of the brewery we choose – the festival beer is good everywhere. By the way, it's a little stronger than the beer usually available, which many newcomers and even more Italians have had to bitterly pay for. Wiesn acquaintances are quickly made and forgotten even faster. Sometimes they end on the slopes of Theresienhöhe in front of the face of Bavaria and sometimes with expulsion from the festival tent. This usually happens when one assumes the server has “given unmistakable signals” and she “really looks great.” Never, really never, should the server be thought of as anything more than she is: the bearer of the beer. Everything else leads to nothing. She is not the festival tent management, not the security, not the cigarette machine, and absolutely not a flirting opportunity.

title: Fichtelberglauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
The Fichtelberg Run takes place in Neudorf in the Ore Mountains.

First the starting signal goes off for all participants of the 9.1 km mountain run. A little later, all mountain bikers start the 6.8 km mountain time trial. There are often around 250 starters on site and every year the organisers SV Neudorf e.V. and RSV Sehmatal e.V. expect a constant number of participants.
story_prologue_title: Conquer the Fichtelberg's Trails of Glory
story_prologue_body: The misty veil lifted from the Fichtelberg mountain range, revealing a challenge that would test even the most seasoned trail runners. The air was alive with anticipation as competitors gathered at the starting line, their eyes fixed on the rugged terrain ahead. For one day only, the best athletes in Germany would clash in the Salomon Trailrunning Cup, and I was about to join their ranks.
story_epilogue_body: As I crossed the finish line, exhausted but exhilarated, I gazed out at the breathtaking Fichtelberg landscape, its peaks still shrouded in mist. The roar of the crowd faded into the distance as I reflected on the journey that had brought me here – nine kilometers of unforgiving terrain, where only the strongest emerged victorious. Though my legs ached and lungs burned, I knew I'd earned every step of this glorious trail.

breakpoints.main_quest_snippet: As I emerged from the mist, the trailhead's signpost beckoned me to begin my journey. The Fichtelberg Trail Cup was about to unfold, and I was ready to take on the best. My racing heart pounded in anticipation as I laced up my shoes and prepared for the grueling test ahead.

The forest swallowed me whole as I plunged into the Pöhlberg Forest Cut. Trees loomed above, their branches creaking in the gentle breeze. The trail narrowed, and I quickened my pace, feeling the weight of competition bearing down on me.

Granite cliffs rose like titans as I crested the Granite Crest Ridge. The wind howled around me, threatening to sweep me off course. But I dug deep, drawing on every last ounce of strength and willpower to push forward.
Fichtelberg Saddle beckoned like an oasis, a respite from the unyielding climb. I collapsed onto a rocky outcropping, gasping for air as the landscape unfolded before me like a map to the summit.

As I reached the Summit Panorama Deck, the wind died down, and an eerie stillness fell over me. The world spread out in breathtaking splendor – a tapestry of mountains, valleys, and lakes that left me awestruck.

title: Path of Love in Bad Oberdorf
short_description:
This small jogging route takes us through Bad Oberdorf over the romantic Path of Love and continues along the Fatherland Trail back to the starting point.

Romantic resting benches, great views, and shady paths await us during this jogging route. Initially, the path leads on the paved road through Bad Oberdorf past typical Allgäu houses. From the very beginning, it steadily climbs uphill to the Prinz-Luitpold-Haus, known for its sulfur springs. On the shady "Path of Love," many benches with engraved poems about the theme of love invite you to rest and reflect. The covered pavilion with views of the Ostrachtal mountains is a nice place to stretch. After crossing a small bridge below the Schleierfall waterfall, wonderful views of the Ostrachtal await us along the Fatherland Trail. The final section leads us along the Ostrach on a shady path back to the starting point.

title: Kyffhäuser Mountain Run - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
The International Kyffhäuser Mountain Run has been based in Frankenhausen since 1979 and has attracted numerous runners ever since.

The range of courses includes various distances: The so-called Kyffhäuser Mountain Marathon is the main race. In addition, distances of 6 km, 14.9 km and the half-marathon distance have to be mastered, whereby everything from running to walking/nordic walking to hiking is permitted. The Salomon Trail Running Cup takes place on the 14.9 km mountain run.

title: Rennsteiglauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
A real highlight is the GutsMuths-Rennsteiglauf, a cross-country run along the Rennsteig in memory of GutsMuths, the co-founder of gymnastics from the Goethe era. This is the largest and possibly also the most beautiful landscape run in Central Europe.

The GutsMuths Rennsteig Run leads along the "Rennsteig" high trail in the Thuringian Forest, a romantic German low mountain range. The run is correspondingly popular: every year around 15,000 runners, Nordic walkers and hikers find their way to the starting point. Especially in East Germany, the event, which has been taking place since the 1970s, has cult status: when the GDR still existed, the run was the largest mass sports event ever. Anyone who could claim to have taken part successfully was highly respected in sporting circles. It is no different today. Possible distances include the super marathon (72.7 km), the marathon (43.5 km), half marathon (21.1 km) and various walking and Nordic walking routes (17, 35, 50 km).

title: Parade of the Wiesn hosts
short_description:
The Munich Wiesn is officially opened each year with the parade of the festival hosts. Watching is an experience!

In 1887, the now traditional parade of the Wiesn hosts took place for the first time. Colorful and magnificently decorated horse-drawn carriages of the breweries, hosts, bartenders, and waitresses are accompanied by the brass bands of the festival tents during their parade and meet around noon at the festival grounds of Munich which marks the official beginning of Oktoberfest. As soon as the festival hosts arrive at the Theresienwiese, the mayor of Munich taps the first beer barrel at exactly 12 noon in the Schottenhamel tent. Together with the shout "O'zapft is" Oktoberfest is officially opened.

title: Hochfelln Mountain Run - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
The international Hochfelln mountain run is an "oldie" that is well attended every year.

The Ski-Club Bergen e.V. regularly organises Germany's oldest mountain run. Athletes, top cross-country skiers, the most successful international mountain sports specialists and well-known athletes from other sports umbrella organisations can compete against each other. But also well-trained non-licensed popular runners (hobby, recreational and amateur athletes) like to take part in the performance comparison and see who has the longer breath. The German classic is held on the 2000 World Cup course (8.9 km, 1,074 metres altitude difference).

title: Kernberglauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
Shortly before the running season comes to an end, the Jena University Sports Association (Universitätssportverein Jena e.V.) organises the Jena Kernberg Run. The programme includes distances of five kilometres (for everyone), 15 kilometres and 27 kilometres.

 

The first Jena Kernberg Run was held in 1975. Whereas in the early days just 20 local residents met to run the race, the number of participants continued to rise over the decades. With the new millennium, there are regularly over 1000 enthusiastic runners every year.

title: Hain-Main-Danube Canal round near Bamberg
short_description:
This varied jogging route takes us from the edge of the cathedral city along the Main-Danube Canal to Strullendorf and back through the Hauptsmoorwald to the starting point at Jahnwiese. The route offers a beautiful combination of forest, meadow, river, and wonderful views of the historic buildings of Bamberg's old town.
We first run into the Hain, Bamberg's city forest. In the Middle Ages, this was a floodplain forest between the two banks of the Regnitz. In 1803, at the request of the Bavarian King Maximilian I Joseph, it was transformed into an artificially created city park based on the model of the English Garden in Munich. A small, idyllic pond in the heart of the Hain is also one of the park's special features. In summer, many fresh-air enthusiasts gather on its shores; in winter, the Hain pond serves as an ice-skating rink. In the adjacent botanical city garden of Bamberg, you can admire a diverse flora during the summer months. Passing numerous small temples, pavilions, and monuments, the path runs along the Regnitz on a forest trail through the tranquil avenues of the Hain. Over the bridge at Buger Spitze and along the Rhine-Main-Danube Canal, we reach the village of Bug—here, several typical Franconian inns invite you to enjoy a cool beer outdoors during the summer months—until reaching Strullendorf. The first plans to build the canal date back to Charlemagne in the year 793. However, the idea was only realized more than 1000 years later with the construction of the Ludwig Canal (1836 and 1846) between Bamberg and Kelheim. After its destruction in World War II, the construction of the current Main-Danube Canal began in 1960. Due to its connection to the Rhine, it forms the link in the continuously navigable inland waterway between the North Sea and the Black Sea. From the canal bank, you have a wonderful panoramic view of the elevations of the Franconian Switzerland in good weather. To our right, we always have the Regnitz and its typical floodplain landscape in sight. In summer, many nature lovers can be seen swimming, sunbathing, cycling, or rowing. From Strullendorf, we return along the opposite bank of the canal toward Bamberg, where we first pass through the main forest of Bamberg and later reach the southern fields. From now on, the entire beauty of Bamberg's old town opens up on the horizon. Besides Bamberg's Altenburg castle, we have fantastic views of numerous historic buildings of the "City of Seven Hills." At the end, we pass the Jako Arena—where Bamberg basketball players play their Bundesliga home games in the impressive hall.

title: Traditional Costume and Shooting Parade Wiesn
short_description:
If you own a festive, complete traditional costume from head to toe, this is the perfect place for you!

In honor of the silver wedding anniversary of King Ludwig I and Therese of Bavaria, a traditional costume parade was held for the first time in Munich in 1835. Since 1950 it has been held annually and is now one of the highlights of the Munich Oktoberfest. On the first Wiesn Sunday, several thousand participants from various traditional costume and shooting clubs parade in their traditional festive attire from the Maximilianeum along a seven-kilometer route through the downtown Munich to the festival grounds at the Theresienwiese. The parade is led by the Münchner Kindl, the Munich coat of arms figure, and is accompanied by brass bands and flag swingers. The clubs and groups mostly come from Bavaria, but also from Austria, Switzerland, and northern Italy.

title: Oberelbe Marathon - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
The RENTA Oberelbe Marathon takes place between Königstein and Dresden - as the name suggests over a distance of 42.195 km. The programme also includes a half marathon, a 10 km run, a 10 km walking course and a 3.7 km mini marathon/company run.

Every year, the Salomon company combines several traditional trail running events in a cup ranking. The running events take place in Germany's most beautiful landscapes and lead over renowned routes such as the already legendary Karwendel route. Once again, running and mental limits are tested as professional runners or ambitious hobby joggers take on one or the other trail under their soles.

title: Schneekopflauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
The Schneekopflauf ends on the summit of the same name, with the last stretch still involving the difference in altitude between 711 m and 978 m.

In 1924, the very first Rennsteiglauf led from the Schneekopf plateau to Schmiedefeld. Today, the route has been reversed by the organisers: now it's 12.7 km from Schmiedefeld via the Großer Finsterberg up to the Schneekopf.

title: Karwendel Mountain Run - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
The legendary Karwendel mountain run celebrates its tenth anniversary in 2010. In addition to the 10.6 km, the runners also have to cover a proud 1381 metres in altitude.

Every year, the Salomon company combines several traditional trail running events in a cup ranking. The running events take place in Germany's most beautiful landscapes and lead over renowned routes such as the already legendary Karwendel route. Once again, running and mental limits are tested as professional runners or ambitious hobby joggers take on one or the other trail under their soles.

title: Tegelberglauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
The run up the Tegelberg is regularly organised by TSV Schwangau and SC Füssen.

Every year, the Salomon company combines several traditional trail running events in a cup ranking. The running events take place in Germany's most beautiful landscapes and lead along renowned routes such as the legendary Karwendel course. Once again, the participants will be able to test their running and mental limits, whether they are professional runners or ambitious hobby joggers, on one or other of the trails.

title: Around the Panzerwiese in Munich
short_description:
"Around the Panzerwiese" is a beautiful running route through a nature reserve that, unlike other parks in Munich, is not crowded with people. Here you can enjoy peace and nature - right on the outskirts of Munich. Football fans will be thrilled by the great view of the Allianz Arena.
The Panzerwiese is a heathland in the north of Munich. The name comes from its former military use. It was only purchased by the city in 1994, although people had enjoyed walking there 20 years earlier. No trees or shrubs grow on the meadow. A total of about 180 plant species have been found there, 23 of which are endangered. The Hartelholz and the Panzerwiese provide habitat not only for flora but also for various animal species, such as the partridge. Here, too, 35 species are already on the Red List. Since 2002, this area has been a nature reserve and has been designated by the EU as a Flora-Fauna Habitat Area. The Panzerwiese is bounded in the north by the Hartelholz, which extends to the A99, in the east by Ingolstädter Straße (B13), in the south by a residential area along Neuherbergstraße and in the west by Schleißheimerstraße. From the Panzerwiese you have a great view of the Allianz Arena. Especially in the evening hours of a game day, the football arena, illuminated in red or blue, is a magnificent sight.

title: Rothaarsteig Marathon - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
The international FALKE-Rothaarsteig Marathon takes place in Fleckenberg in the Schmallenberg Sauerland.

In addition to the marathon, which is part of the Trailrunning Cup, the course programme also includes a half marathon. This can also be completed in the disciplines of walking and Nordic walking.

title: Hochgratlauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description:
This run is designed for ambitious runners. In addition to a professional organisation, the Hochgratberglauf impresses with the great panorama of Bavaria and unique nature experiences are guaranteed. This run is a mixture of amateur and professional sport, where hobby runners can compete with top athletes.

The start of the run is the Hochgratbahn valley station at 858m above sea level. The finish is at 1708m altitude and is the Hochgratbahn mountain station. The total length of the route is 6040m with a difference in altitude of 850m. From the start, the course runs for about 2000m on an asphalt road that is about four metres wide. The rest of the route is a mountain path about 2 metres wide. In wet road and path conditions, running shoes with non-slip soles should be used.

title: Hochwald Gourmet Marathon Saarbrücken
short_description:
Whether for Sunday joggers, marathon pros, or spectators – the Gourmet Marathon Saarbrücken is a delight in many ways.

At the Hochwald Gourmet Marathon there is a flat, officially measured 10.55 km loop course through the most beautiful streets of the state capital Saarbrücken. The marathon route is run four times and the half marathon twice. In the team relay, each member of the 4-person team runs the loop once. The mini marathon is completed on a partial section.

title: Rennsteiglauf Marathon Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: Before the starting signal is given in Neuhaus on the large meadow on the Apelberg (820 m above sea level), there is singing and swaying. It's a tradition - no marathoner sets off without a "snow waltz" - a unique atmosphere that is second to none. With the starting signal, WSV Neuhaus then releases around 3,200 starters every year through the large 4-metre wide starting gate on their way of 43.5 km to Schmiedefeld. For the time being, the route goes from the wide meadow to the "narrow" road out of Neuhaus. Almost 6 kilometres must be run on the road until, after the first refreshment stop at "Sandwieschen" (km 5.81 / 777 m NN), the trail enters the forest. At kilometre 10.63 you will reach the first refreshment point "Dreistromstein" (812 m), which is run by WSV Scheibe-Alsbach. Freshly refreshed, the route continues over ascents and descents to the "Eisfelder Ausspanne" (km 15.76 / 752 m) and from there uphill to the highest point of the marathon course, the "Eselsberg" (km 18.8 / 841 m) with its tower hut, a landmark of the Rennsteig. A refreshment point has been set up here by the SG "Rennsteig" Masserberg and an intermediate time is taken. The route now descends. When you cross the road (km 19.75 / 785), you have already climbed 56 m. Pass the meadow behind Masserberg and head towards the next refreshment point, the "Schwalbenhaupt" (km 22.7 / 703 m), where the Schleusegrund Hiking Club serves refreshments. But be careful. Before reaching the refreshment point, the trail descends through a sunken path over sticks, roots and stones. A real cross-country run. Parallel to the road, the Rennsteig leads in the direction of Neustadt, past the car park of the Altenfeld ski lift. Here you have reached kilometre 25. When Neustadt comes into view, first cross the road in Kahlert and continue along the Rennsteig to the entrance to Neustadt/petrol station. Walk through the town to the church. There you turn left to reach the Neustadt running group's aid station (km 29.2 / 805 m). Freshly fortified, you can now take the climb over the Großer Burgberg (818 m). It is a steep climb, mostly taken at a walk. But it is not far to the next refreshment point at the "Dreiherrenstein" (Km 34.3 / 810 m), run by IG Stützerbach. From there it's a gentle downhill to Frauenwald. At the "Monument am Bohrstuhl" (Km 38.23 / 786 m), the Frauenwälder SV awaits the runners with a final refreshment. Those who want to can also get a "sip" of Köstritzer Schwarzbier here as an energy boost for the last kilometres to Schmiedefeld. Schmiedefeld, the finish - cross the level crossing and turn left into the "Reitallee" (Km 42,59 / 622 m). A final climb to the sports field at 711 m - the acid test for every marathoner who would have already reached the finish in a normal marathon. You can already hear the hustle and bustle from the finish. Surrounded by many spectators cheering you on for the last few metres, everyone gives it their last. Then another half lap of the stadium and you're at the finish. You have completed the 43.5 kilometre Rennsteiglauf Marathon and a 1.4 kilometre marathon cross.

title: Bike route Sonthofen-Iller source (Oberstdorf)
short_description:
A pleasant bike route along the cool Iller to the Iller source

We start at the station square of Sonthofen and ride along Bahnhofsstraße, turn right into Moltkestraße. At the end of the street (30 km/h zone) we turn right into Immenstädter Straße. We reach an underpass and ride through it. We keep left and ride up towards Illerdam. We reach Illerdam and turn left towards Altstädten. We follow the signs always towards Oberstdorf-Iller source.

title: Hike to Schoimosch Castle
short_description:
A short hike to Schoimosch Castle.

The hike to Schoimosch Castle leads us to a special viewpoint (overlooking the town of Lipova and the Marosch river) marked by history.

title: "Cross Youth" Competition
short_description:
Parcul Tineretului din Capitală va găzdui miercuri, 7 mai, „Crosul Tineretului“, un eveniment destinat iubitorilor de sport. Cei care vor lua parte la competiţie vor putea pleca acasă cu numeroase premii.

„Crosul Tineretului” se va desfăşura în Parcul Tineretului şi se adresează persoanelor iubitoare de sport. Pentru a participa la competiţie concurenţii trebuie să se înscrie la unul din punctele situate pe platoul de la intrarea în parcul Tineretului - B-dul Şincai, pe mai multe categorii de vârstă. Ministerul Tineretului şi Sportului invită bucureştenii să participe la eveniment în număr cât mai mare pentru a încuraja sportul de masă. „Voi participa cu toată bucuria la Crosul Tineretului. Vreau să fiu alături de tineri, vreau să alergăm împreună pentru sănătate, pentru energie şi aş vrea să fie alături de noi cât mai mulţi bucureşteni. De aceea, îi invit pe toţi la „Crosul Tineretului” să alerge şi să se bucure.”, Gabriela SZABO, Ministrul Tineretului şi Sportului. Înscrierea concurenţilor se va face în ziua evenimentului, 7 mai 2014, în zona special amenajată din Intrarea Parcul Tineretului - B-dul Şincai, între orele 8:00-10:00, la punctele special amenajate pentru fiecare categorie de participanţi. Concurenţii trebuie să fie apţi fizic pentru a alerga la „Crosul Tineretului” , pe o distanţă de aproximativ 3 kilometri. ”Crosul Tineretului” este un eveniment ce face parte din proiectul ”Zilele Tineretului”, desfăşurate între 2-9 mai 2014.

title: FlaemingSkate bike and skate route (route 1)
short_description:
A route tailored specifically to the needs of cyclists and inline skaters in Brandenburg. Good asphalt conditions, no cars, and flexible division of stages with different difficulty levels make this route suitable for both families and endurance athletes.

The FlaemingSkate bike and skate route (route 1) is one of the athletic attractions in the region. The various entry points to the route are clearly visible and marked with "Flaeming Skate." Along the way, there are many sights such as various BMX trails, castles, monuments, and, of course, the idyllic forests of the region. At nearly 100 km, this route is the longest continuous route of its kind in Europe. There are plenty of accommodation options along the way to suit every budget.

title: Hike to the 7 Colored Earth in Chamarel, Mauritius
short_description:
The route leads past sugar cane fields, coffee plantations, and the Chamarel waterfall to the 7 Colored Earth, one of the main attractions of Mauritius.

The 2.3 km long hiking trail is very flat and therefore suitable for everyone. Unfortunately, the natural spectacle is privately owned, so we have to pay a small entrance fee at the parking lot. The first highlight of our hike is the Chamarel waterfall. There, the small rivers St Denis and Viande Salée plunge 100 m down. Opposite is a viewing platform from which we have a very good view of the waterfall. In the gorge, we can see two different lava layers, dating from approximately 1.7 to 3.5 and 8 to 10 million years ago. Especially spectacular is the cascade during cyclone season (December to April). During this time, the two rivers carry many times more water. We can also experience the waterfall up close. For this, we have to leave our path before the viewing platform at a right turn. The small path then leads directly to the river and the gorge. After taking enough photos of the waterfall, we return to the trail. It leads us directly to our second big highlight, the 7 Colored Earth, also called Colored Earth or Colored Land. There, the earth shimmers in seven different colors, from red to blue to green. This is the result of the complete leaching of basalts and chemical reactions of metals with water. Through a small circular walk, we can view the earth from all sides. But the earth is not the only experience. Right next to it are several exotic plants and an enclosure with giant tortoises. After a refreshment in the restaurant, we set off on the return journey. Perhaps we will enjoy the view of Cascade Chamarel, as the waterfall is also called, once again or stop by the sugar cane fields to briefly talk with the friendly workers, provided one understands French, which is the official language of Mauritius.

title: Ilmenau bike route Lüneburg Heath
short_description:
A beautiful, multi-day bike route along the Ilmenau river in the Lüneburg Heath.

The approx. 120 km of this bike route leads us in four stages along the Ilmenau river from Bad Bodenteich in the south of the Lüneburg Heath to just before Hamburg to Winsen. The paths mostly run through the FFH protected area Ilmenau, where rare birds and plants can be experienced. The well-signposted route is designed as a nature experience bike trail and runs mostly on paved roads, but also partly on longer unpaved sections through the relatively flat landscape of the Lüneburg Heath.

title: Mulderadweg - Vereinte Mulde
short_description:
An easy, mostly flat route that can be ridden in one or several days. We cycle 122 km through the Mulde Valley in Saxony-Anhalt to Dessau.

 

Can be done individually or as a connecting route to the Mulderadweg - Freiberger Mulde or Mulderadweg - Zwickauer Mulde. The Mulderadweg is not an artificially created cycle path. It runs on little-trafficked public roads and partly on hiking trails. The area around the cycle path is also called the “Valley of Castles” due to the many castles and ruins.

title: Mulderadweg - Freiberger Mulde
short_description:
An easy to moderate route with gentle ascents, which can be completed in one or several days, covering a length of 106 km.

This route is one of two "feeder routes" to the Mulderadweg - United Mulde. On this route, we follow from the Czech border the fastest river in Europe along side roads, bike paths, forest and field paths.

title: Regnitz Cycle Path - Valley Route
short_description:
This simple river route is well signposted and runs along idyllic paths beside the Pegnitz and Regnitz rivers through Franconia.

 

The cycle path, divided into four stages, runs for 85 km along the Pegnitz and Regnitz. We ride without major climbs on side roads and farm tracks and experience both the nature and culture of the region. Since the route mostly runs on paved streets with little traffic, it is especially suitable for family routes.

title: Around the Hallertau
short_description:
The approximately 215 km long circular route in the greater Ingolstadt area runs on flat paths along smaller and larger rivers.

There are few small inclines on the cycling route in the Pfaffenhofen district. The path mostly runs along bike paths or little-trafficked side roads and is therefore well suited for families.

title: Rhine Cycle Route - from Lustenau to Basel
short_description:
On this almost 250 km long long-distance cycle route, we follow the course of the Rhine from the Austrian-Swiss border almost to the French border in Basel.

This cycle route is part of the trans-European Rhine Cycle Route, which runs through the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland. As one of nine stages, we cycle this route from Germany almost all the way to France. Through a scenically unique region, this long-distance cycle route first goes along the shores of Lake Constance on steadily descending paths and then follows the course of the Rhine on little-used side roads and cycle paths all the way to Basel.

title: From the Devil's Moor to the Wadden Sea
short_description:
This 450 km long circular cycle route leads through the typical landscape of the north. Over many lakes, rivers and finally also past the sea, this route takes us once around nature reserves and tourist regions;

Those who read the name of the tour will not fail to notice that this tour leads through the so-called Devil's Moor, a moorland area of more than 600 square metres. This title, however, only hints at one of the many landscapes we cross on this long-distance cycle route. On mostly asphalted and only in a few places gravel roads we cycle on mostly traffic-free roads and paths. The region between the North Sea and the rivers Elbe and Weser is characterised by moorland, small villages and the large urban centres of the north such as Cuxhaven, Bremerhaven and of course Bremen;

title: Weser-Harz-Heide long-distance cycle route (Bokel-Ebstorf-Lüneburg)
short_description:
The almost 76 km long section of the Weser-Harz-Heide long-distance cycle route leads through the Lüneburg Heath on minor roads with little traffic in places and on gravel paths in others. ei

On this route we cycle through the peaceful landscape of Südheide. We pass special features such as the Hösseringen museum village and cultural highlights such as the Ebstorf monastery and the Hundertwasser railway station on paths that climb moderately from time to time but are mostly asphalted until we reach Lüneburg.

title: Wümme Cycle Route
short_description:
This cycle path in the Bremen catchment area runs for almost 260 km, always close to the river Wurm. Over roads with little traffic and through impressive moorland, you cycle partly in Lower Saxony and partly in Bremen through the foothills of the Lüneburger Heide.

On this trail we cycle on mostly flat, asphalted terrain along a well-signposted, low-traffic route. The tour can be divided up and is also suitable for day trips. In the nature reserve of the Lüneburger Heide, through which the cycle route runs, there are many places of interest and places to stop for refreshments. Here the paths are a little more demanding and no longer asphalted throughout;

title: Along the Ligurian coast
short_description: Leisurely cycling on the 25 km long, flat cycle path from Sanremo to San Lorenzo with fantastic coastal stretches.

title: Chasseral - The Queen of the Jura
short_description:
A very nice tour over the Chasseral and along the ridge with nice views over the lake of Biel. On a sunny day there are some amazing views of the Alps in the distance.

Chasseral is a great day out for those who like their mountain biking to take in long sections of single track and don’t mind a bit of climbing to get it. Most routes that I have seen described for Chasseral begin near the lake of Biel (Bielersee) and climb the southern side of Chasseral. For our route we took the train from Biel to Cormoret and ascended from the north side. This cut out a few hundred metres of climbing and allowed us to take a quite pleasant (for the most part) and not very steep route to the top.

title: Col de Cou (The Brazilian)
short_description:
The trail from Col de Cou to the Rhone Valley via Nax has become one of the classic trails in the Swiss Alps. It got named "The Brazilian" by some journalists who came here to ride it a number of years back, but the locals have been riding it for a long time before it got international aclaim and a "cool" name.

Col de Cou is a must do for all mountain bikers based in Switzerland. It's reputation precedes it and the almost 2000m of singletrail descent in gives it an almost legendary status. This trail is typical Wallis. It's been ridden a lot in the last few years and has suffered a little due to this, but some of the character does still exist. From Col de Cou the trail first descends over Alpine Meadows before dropping into the Woods and then finally swooping it's way down to the Rhone valley after passing Nax. This is one to get out and enjoy...

title: Creux du Van
short_description:
Creux du Van is located in the Swiss Jura and is a spectacular cliff in the shape of a huge amphitheater. The limestone landscape rises from Lake Neuchatel and the Travers Valley, which is famous for absinthe. This route leads from the Travers Valley to Lake Travers and goes over Creux du Van.

Creux du Van is a UNESCO world heritage site in the Canton of Jura. The limestone landscape rises from the Lake of Neuchatel and the Travers Valley which is famous for Absinthe. This tour crosses from the Travers valley to the lake taking in the natural amphitheater at Creux du Van.

title: Varnerwald
short_description:
A nice scenic tour with a long and very flowy trail above the Rhone valley to Varen followed by an XC trail along the Bisse (waterway) back to Sierre.

This is a very nice singletrail tour with some nice views over the Walliser Alps and the Rhone valley. The tour climbs on at a fairly easy gradient to the start of the single trail which is gauranteed to get pretty much everyone smiling. The return to Sierre is on an old irrigation channel that is still used to bring water to the vineyards in the valley.

title: Juniper trail in the Oberbergischer juniper heath near Eckenhagen
short_description:
On the circular hiking route, you can discover one of the last remaining juniper heaths.

The 5.5 km long circular hiking route leads through the Branscheider juniper heath and provides information along the way with signs about the importance of juniper.

title: Rochers de Naye
short_description:
Short but technically demanding tour with views over lake Geneva and the surrounding mountains.

The Rochers de Naye (2042) is the highest railway in the Canton Vaud and provides you with easy access to a 1500m descent with the majority of it on moderately technical singletrail. The top of the route is quite high alpine in nature and does feature some exposure in places. The upper high alpine section is split from the lower woodland section by a couple of kilometers of fire road. The woodland section is quite tight and narrow and requires good brake control. The lowest section of the trail features a number of switchbacks which had been straighlined the last time we rode the route. Please respect the trail and do not take shortcuts. On weekends there is likely to be a lot of hikers on the top sections of the trail.

title: International Art Hiking Trail Hoher Fläming – Southern Route
short_description:
Varied art hiking route with 17 art stations on the theme "Settlement of Fläming by people from Flanders" by six German and six Flemish artists from Belgium and the Netherlands

The southern route of the International Art Hiking Trail runs without major elevation changes between Wiesenburg and Bad Belzig. Along the route, cow herds graze peacefully in the meadow, a pack of wolves has returned to the Fläming, and the Resting Bridge turns everything upside down. The art hiking trail invites not only to hike but also to wonder. Some artworks are monumental, others delicate and poetic. The southern route of the International Art Hiking Trail covers a wide spectrum of modern art and passes a total of 17 artworks, which can be discovered in beautiful forests and small villages, on flowery meadows, or sometimes right in the middle of a village pond. Twelve of these artworks were installed along the route in 2010 as part of a German-Belgian-Dutch competition. Along the way, there are many beautiful views over the hilly landscape crowned by majestic castles and fortresses.

title: Along the Iller past the Ortwanger See

title: Rhine route Duisburg
short_description:
For an approximately one-hour jogging route, the Duisburg districts of Homberg and Baerl are recommended. On both sides of the Rhine, you can mostly run on the dike crown, sometimes paved, but mostly gravel. You cross the Rhine twice and have a nice circular course away from the urban center.

On both sides of the Rhine, you can do either a small hike or a jogging route on the dike crown. The jogging route lasts about an hour for the average trained person. The jogging route offers a view of the beginning of the green Lower Rhine, but on the right Rhine side you see the relics of Duisburg's old steel past: the right Rhine side is characterized by ThyssenKrupp, which you can discover, among other places, in Duisburg-Homberg at the old Thyssen power plant. Moving on the right Rhine side and looking at the left, you already get an impression of how the landscape increasingly dominates downstream towards the Netherlands. All in all, a very nice regeneration route after a strenuous workday.

title: Training Round Allgäu SwimRun
short_description:
The short training course for the Allgäu SwimRun is a circuit that can be run as often as desired. With a one-kilometre swim and five-kilometre run, the course is also suitable for beginners.

The training loop starts at the large car park for hikers on the southern shore of the Niedersonthofener See lake. After a leisurely flat roll-in on the path running alongside the road, the few positive metres of the loop follow. At the highest point of the route we follow the signs to the right towards the lake. From here we leave the asphalt roads and take a wide gravel road to the next small hamlet, where we turn right towards the campsite. However, we go around this on the left in the direction of the boat rental or bathing area. This is where the first swim starts to the bathing area of Niedersonthofener See, further to the south, on the other side of the lake. Back on land, follow the wide hiking trail for about 1.5 km along the shore to start the second swim at a "wild" entrance. The crossing of the lake to the bathing area on the opposite side is the longer of the two swims at about 700 metres. Back on land, you can start the second lap directly or walk back towards the car park.

title: Remstecken Koblenz
short_description:
This beautiful jogging route, which is not particularly demanding, is suitable for anyone with a little fitness and jogging experience. The route is a five-minute drive from Koblenz city centre.

The tour leads almost exclusively through woodland and at the beginning even a short stretch on the Rheinburger-Höhenweg. There is a magnificent view of the Moselle valley at one point.

title: After-work route through Steig and Unterried
short_description:
This easy jogging route contains hardly any inclines, runs exclusively over asphalt and gravel paths, and is therefore well suited as an after-work route.

The route is ideal for recharging your energy after a stressful workday and enjoying the silence in the small villages of Steig and Unterried. It passes idyllically located farms, a wet meadow with rare plant species, and through a bright forest.

title: Jogging route via Blaichach
short_description:
We enjoy a varied, moderate jogging route from Immenstadt via the Rieder-Alp and Schwanden into Blaichach. Returning along the Iller.

Shortly after the start, a first strenuous climb awaits us. Behind the Riederalp, we go down a long staircase until it climbs steeply again after Schwanden. Here we reach the highest point of the route. It then goes steadily downhill to the Blaichach station. On the way back to Immenstadt, the terrain along the Iller is almost flat. Here you can choose depending on your mood to enter a pleasant to strenuous steady running pace.

title: Up to Alpe Gund
short_description:
We enjoy a challenging mountain run up to Alpe Gund, which, however, repeatedly offers flatter sections to catch our breath.

On the ascent, we follow forest or forest roads. Only the sections from the cemetery to the Wooden Chapel and from Almagmach to the Mittelbergalpe feature strong to very steep climbs. For the descent back into the Steigbach valley, we use a wonderful hiking trail that advises less experienced mountain runners to be cautious.

title: Forest Educational Trail «Allmendhölzli»
short_description: On the predefined one-hour round tour, 14 different tree species and 7 problem areas of forest cultivation are being presented. You will also find an invitable fire place. EA survey by the Cantonal Forestry Office of Zurich on the population's wishes regarding the woods showed a great need for recreational forest close to nature. Therefore, this forest educational trail was created by the Allmend Wood Corporation of Horgen in spring 1999, in close cooperation with Horgen's forest enterprise and the Cantonal Forestry Office of Zurich. The following topics are treated: 1. Start 2. Larch 3. Walnut Tree 4. Nectria ditissima cancer of beech 5. Yew Tree 6. Hornbeam 7. Protective functions 8. Spruce 9. Norway Maple 10. Silver Fir rejuvenation 11. Shelterwood system rejuvenation 12. Pine 13. Ivy 14. Cherry Tree 15. Blackberry Problem 16. Fire places 17. Oak Tree 18. Douglas Fir 19. Beech 20. title: Chlustobel trail Weissbad – Brülisau
short_description:
Experience with all your senses the exciting and original Chlustobel along the Brüelbach between Weissbad and Brülisau.

Have you ever taken a stone from a stream, turned it over, and observed what clings to it or hurriedly crawls away? Can you guess how many creatures your feet are standing on right now? Join us on an exploration journey into the unknown familiar! Keep your eyes and nose open, sharpen your ears, and let your senses run free. Dive into the mysterious Chlustobel! The nature experience trail is suitable for young and old alike. On five panels, information about the nature of the Chlustobel and its inhabitants is presented. Short instructions encourage exciting observations and fun games. You should allow yourself two to three hours for the path if you want to experience the information and observations.

title: Cultural walk Fischingen
short_description: The cultural walk connects the rich offer of monuments of national importance around Fischingen: Fischingen Monastery, St. Martin's Chapel in Oberwangen, the Church of the Holy Cross and St. Mary's Church in Dussnang and St. Anna Church in Au. The walk starts at Fischingen Monastery. To get to the St. Anna Church in Au, first follow the main road in a southerly direction. Leave the main road immediately after the stream crossing and take the narrow asphalt road on the left. The road then climbs steadily until you reach the "Neuschür" farm. From there, the pilgrims' path continues straight ahead on the gravel path and then through the forest. Along the stream, it becomes narrower and narrower until you emerge from the forest again at the hamlet of Au. On the right hand side, on the other side of the main road, you can see the St. Anna church. The same path leads back to Fischingen Monastery. For the second part of the walk, first follow the main road northwards through the village of Fischingen. At the end of the village, the pilgrims' path branches off to the right and then immediately left onto a field path. This leads first across the meadow and then along the edge of the forest. A bridge helps the hiker to cross the Murg, along which the path continues. After the barbecue site (on the other side of the stream), you leave the Murg and the forest and enter the village of Dussnang. Pass the sports field on the left and then turn right on the main road towards the centre of the village. At the next crossroads you will find the Kreuzkirche and the Marienkirche. You follow the road along the Marienkirche, through the whole village, always heading east, back over the main road and the Murg to the district of Oberwangen. Even from a distance, you can see the St. Martin's Chapel on the small hill. To get on the path to Fischingen Monastery, go back a few steps and then follow the pilgrims' path again. This rises steadily and leads through the forest, past the forest nature trail to the clearing with the Fischingen special school. Follow the asphalted road downhill, then take the right-hand bend and immediately turn left up into the forest. Now follow the pilgrims' path through the Schlyffitobel back to the Fischingen monastery. Note(s) The easiest way to reach Fischingen is by bus from Sirnach every hour. title: Ziit-Spuure, short tour
short_description: Fehraltorf is not only an up-and-coming agglomeration community of Zurich. Our village has a long and eventful history, which has also left its traces in many houses. In recent years, the Nature and Heritage Conservation Commission has provided many of these contemporary witnesses with an information board (Ziit-Spuure board). Experience Fehraltorf from a new perspective. Take your time for the "Ziit-Spuuren" of our community, first of all for a small tour through our village. From the railway station SBB Fehraltorf (Ziit-Spuure plate 8), the starting point of the small tour, only a few steps lead us along Bahnhofstrasse to Migros. The Glogg & Co. shoe factory (Ziit-Spuure plate 7), once the largest employer in the village with over 100 jobs, stood on this spot until 1985. We walk on and come to the property at Bahnhofstrasse 10, an inconspicuous residential building. In the 19th century, a public bath was located here (Ziit-Spuure plate 9). On the right, a few steps towards the village, is the Reformed vicarage built in the 19th century (Ziit-Spuure plate 6). On a cul-de-sac, which branches off at a right angle to the right two houses further on, we find the Mettlen kindergarten, the first municipal kindergarten of the then primary school community (Ziit-Spuure plate 41). Among the 38 children (a few of the class are missing in the photo due to illness) are 5 cousins from the same family. Right next door are the factory buildings of the Schellenberg textile printing works (Ziit-Spuure plates 40a, 40b). At Kempttalstrasse 68, in the immediate vicinity of the roundabout, stands the building of the Zürcher Kantonalbank (Ziit-Spuure Plate 27). It unmistakably dates from a time when banks employed many more employees at their outstations. On Russikerstrasse we reach the second former shoe factory in Fehraltorf (Russikerstrasse 37, Ziit-Spuure plate 37). We continue walking and come to the site of the former Ernst Schütz Kies & Beton AG (Ziit-Spuure plate 46), where the Vivaldi housing development is now located. We continue to the Heiget kindergarten (Ziit-Spuure Tafel 42) and the Heiget Huus (Ziit-Spuure Tafel 13), today's centre for events of all kinds. The Fehraltorf school facilities consist, in simplified form, of the Heiget upper school building (Ziit-Spuure panel 11) and the Heiget primary school facility (Ziit-Spuure panel 12). We cross Rumlikerstrasse and arrive at the terraced single-family houses with the house numbers Sagenrainstrasse 17. The Berghof, originally a farm where the founder of the Unterstrass Seminary, Heinrich Bachofner, grew up, used to stand on this site (Ziit-Spuure Plate 29). After a long walk past the new "Im Berg" development, we reach the farmhouse "Zur Frohen Aussicht", a former restaurant with its own brewery (Ziit-Spuure plate 20). Via the Müliquartier or along Kempttalstrasse we reach Obermüli, originally a mill with water wheel, later a silk twisting mill (today's building dates from this time), today a commercial property. Via Unterdorfstrasse we come to the former Restaurant National (Ziit-Spuure Tafel 19), today the headquarters of the Wirnsberg companies. Right next door used to be the lower Sennhütte, converted into a farmhouse after the merger of the upper and lower Sennhütte (Ziit-Spuure Plate 43), today there are 2 apartment buildings on this site. The tour ends here. Via Staldenbachweg, Obermülistrasse and lower Bahnhofstrasse, the starting point, Fehraltorf SBB railway station, can be easily reached again on foot. Note(s) Walk, also suitable for children and families. short_description:
This jogging route from Trebiano Magra to Lerici leads through partly wooded landscape and past scattered houses.

title: Jogging route around the Niedersonthofener See
short_description:
Once all the way around the Niedersonthofener See: The jogging route offers beautiful views of the water and the Allgäu mountain peaks in the south.

Always with the Niedersonthofener See in sight, we run here a beautiful route that mostly runs over pleasant gravel paths. The inclines are gentle, and the nature around the lake is wonderful at any time of year. Passing the "Insel Campingplatz," we pass the pretty white Guardian Angel Chapel before going between Mitterinselsee and Oberinselsee. Nearby, the jogger enjoys the view of small boats rocking in the shallow water; here is the small boat harbor of the Oberinselsee. After a slight incline, we are rewarded with a great panoramic view over the lake towards the southwest. The south side of Niedersonthofener See is forested: here we enjoy a run directly along the water through the woods.

title: Stelvio Marathon

The original route of the Stelvio Marathon is challenging but offers an unforgettable experience with the legendary Stilfserjoch Pass road and the view of the imposing Ortler group. Those who want to skip the initial kilometers around Prad can choose the Classic route, which is continuously signposted over its 26 kilometers.

The Schottweg trail directly along the Oybach stream is particularly beautiful: The turquoise waters of the wild mountain stream and the high alpine surroundings should not be passed without an extensive photo stop.

In the museum, the history of the brine and the moor is impressively explained. Finally, a waterfall - what more could a hiker's heart desire. (Source: Chiemgau-Tourismus.de)

title: City, country, river
short_description:
This tour is for anyone who wants to explore the bigger side of Berlin and its little neighbour Potsdam. It takes you across and along the Havel River, past picturesque chapels, historic sites and through classic Potsdam.

This tour is for anyone who wants to explore the bigger side of Berlin and its little neighbour Potsdam.

The tour starts at Wannsee S-Bahn station (A) and begins with a ride on the BVG ferry across Wannsee (B). However, this is not really a lake at all, but a large bulge in the Havel. Once you reach the other side, you find yourself at the so-called Imchen (C). The small yacht harbour belongs to the district of Kladow, a lovely former fishing village that is not as famous as Wannsee, but at least as beautiful. After the relaxed ride across the river, it is now really strenuous, because to get to the village you have to pedal up a high Havel hill. Once you reach the top, you pass fields and the village streets of Kladow in the direction of the lake. To get there, the route crosses Kladower Forst, where you can also take a nice break and visit the picturesque Schilffdachkapelle (D). The route runs along both lakes and crosses the Berlin Wall Trail again and again. Finally, you reach the small village of Sacrow, where there is a cute café (F) that invites you to take a break. Then you continue to the castle park and the beautiful Heilandskirche (G), from where you have a good view of the Havel. The colonnade that runs around the little chapel is a particularly nice photo opportunity. Once you're back on the saddle, the tour continues towards Potsdam. The Brandenburg capital enchants with its classicist streetscape and invites you to linger in its many small cafés. Potsdam's old town, with its long pedestrian zone, is also well worth a visit and only a short detour away. The tour then continues via the Glinickerbrücke (L), where agents were exchanged during the division of Germany, back to Berlin. A bit of a hike, but also very beautiful and worth the effort, you reach the Wannsee S-Bahn station again after going up and down the Havel river.

title: Karwendelhaus to Jenbach by MTB
short_description:
Beautiful mountain bike route through the Karwendel Alpine Park including great mountain panoramas, crystal-clear streams, and excellent places to stop for refreshments.
The route then leads past Lake Achensee to Jenbach.

From the Karwendelhaus, there is a gentle climb towards Grasslegerbichl and from there on a forest road partly covered with loose gravel-like surface towards Ahornboden. At higher speeds, this will shake you quite a bit. After arriving at the small Ahornboden, follow the path further downhill to the Rissbach. There, the field path turns into an asphalt road for a few kilometers. You follow this road upstream until a signpost indicates the turnoff to the Plumsjochhütte . From there, it goes steadily uphill to the Plumsjochhütte, which invites you for a short break. From the Plumsjochhütte, it’s a little further to the highest point of the route, the Plumssattel. There you follow the single trail to the Gasthof Gernalm . The first part of the descent is quite steep and features some tight turns. Since there is very loose scree on the path, you should choose a moderate speed as the braking distances are correspondingly long. From the Gernalm, follow the asphalt road downhill and on a nice day you can still take a quick dip in Lake Achensee . Then, along the lake, it goes via the federal road to Jenbach and there towards the train station where this route ends.

title: Stage 01: Between Andermatt and Oberwald
short_description:
The "Rhone Route" is the name of the VéloRoute that crosses Switzerland along the river of the same name. Together with its French equivalent, the "ViaRhôna", they form EuroVélo 17, a magnificent route that links the imposing mountains of the Swiss Alps to the gentle shores of the Mediterranean.
The Rhône Route first crosses the Valais, the sunniest region of Switzerland, with its mountains and pastures. Then you reach the castles of Sion and the vineyards and orchards of the lower Rhone valley. The Route then makes a large arc on the shores of Lake Geneva, via the picturesque terraced vineyards of Lavaux, listed as a World Heritage Site, joining in particular the towns of Montreux, Lausanne and Geneva.
This route is about 350km long, and if the sections are adaptable according to your desires and capacities, we present it here in 8 stages. The Rhone Route - Stage 1: between Andermatt and Oberwald This 1st stage is undoubtedly the most difficult, with the ascent of the Furka Pass, at 2430 metres above sea level. Before that we will have crossed the treeless pastures of the Urseren valley, and after the pass a very fast descent along the glaciers will take us towards Oberwald.

The " Route du Rhône " is the name of the VéloRoute that runs through Switzerland along the river of the same name. Together with its French counterpart, the " ViaRhôna ", they form EuroVélo 17, a magnificent itinerary that links the imposing mountains of the Swiss Alps to the gentle shores of the Mediterranean.
The Rhone Route first crosses the Valais, the sunniest region of Switzerland, with its mountains and pastures. Then you reach the castles of Sion and the vineyards and orchards of the lower Rhone valley. The Route then makes a large arc on the shores of Lake Geneva, via the picturesque terraced vineyards of Lavaux, listed as a World Heritage Site, joining in particular the towns of Montreux, Lausanne and Geneva.
This route is about 350km long, and if the sections are adaptable according to your desires and capacities, we present it here in 8 stages. The Rhone Route - Stage 8 : between Geneva and Chancy This last Swiss stage of the Rhone Route takes you from Geneva to the French-Swiss border. We will have taken the time to appreciate the calm of Geneva, its old streets, its harbour and its 140m high water jet, but also its stereotypes.

title: The Bob Graham Round
short_description:
The Bob Graham Round is a 66-mile, 27,000 foot circuit of 42 of the highest peaks in the English Lake District - to be completed within 24 hours.

First done way back in 1932 by Bob Graham, hotelier of Keswick, at the age of 42, the 42 Peak Round has become a testing ground for the supremely fit. The Bob Graham Round is a 65-66 mile*, 27,000 foot circuit of 42 of the highest peaks in the English Lake District within 24 hours. First done way back in 1932 by Bob Graham, hotelier of Keswick, Cumberland, at the age of 42, the 42 Peak Round has become a testing ground for the supremely fit. Each summer around 100 of the most highly tuned ultra-distance fell runners will attempt the 27,000 ft of ascent within the allotted 24 hours. The Bob Graham round of 42 Lake District fells traversed within 24 hours is probably the most demanding test of physical fitness available to British Athletes or mountaineers. The rules for the Bob Graham 24 hour club state that the round can be attempted either clockwise or anti-clockwise. provided that the start and finish is at Moot Hall, Keswick. http://www.bobgrahamclub.co.uk/ * The early pioneers settled on a figure of 72 miles with 27,000 feet of ascent. The use of mapping software and GPS devices has led to a re-evaluation of the distance of the 42 Peak Round. Mapping software gives figures as low as 61-63 miles. GPS systems (which have been carried and operated throughout several successful attempts) give a figure of between 65-66 miles
